column1: # relation constraint, sited on the FIELD the way the sizing atoms sit
# on containers. Its value may be one address, a LIST of addresses, or a
# MAP whose string leaves are addresses; the container shapes are
# rewritten leaf by leaf through the link machinery, so pending
# resolution, type flow and link stamping are the one battle-tested
# path, and the data side stays plain strings.
# The PREDICATE of every edge produced is the key the relate() sits on --
# declared once, in the schema, never inferred from the path.
# An address is a TREE PATH (ADR-014): `$.a.b` from the root, `.b` from
# the link's own sibling scope. A bare word is NOT an address -- it is
# just a string -- which is why every address here is written as one.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).
# A graph atom beside the relation carries its value, links and templates
# A constraint met with relate() meets the relation's value as any meet does,
# so a string constraint refuses a list; one on each address is the
# value's spread, which also holds a leaf a later list brings, as a link.
# A spread that can hold a container keeps its elements as they come.
# A RELATIVE address in a relate() is resolved at the LEAF's own position,
# so a schema applied by a spread gives each destination its own edge.
